<details open>

CUDA: fix ADD_ID launch for more than 65535 tokens (#33162)

The grid's y dimension came directly from the token count, so ADD_ID
launches with more than 65535 tokens failed with "invalid configuration
argument". NVIDIA and HIP are equally affected, since gridDim.y is
capped at 65535 on both.

Clamp the grid and stride over ne2 in the kernel, matching convert.cu
and pad.cu. Add a test case at 70000 tokens; the existing cases top out
at 129.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5

</details>

items.body:
<details open>

vulkan: further optimize coopmat2 GDN (#32860)

* vulkan: further optimize coopmat2 GDN

Refactor split+store callbacks so hi and lo portions are all stored together.
This should help allow the stores to be vectorized.

Interleave the state store callbacks with the gram_pmat work. The compiler
doesn't seem to let these things overlap without manual effort like this. I
suspect this is because the compiler doesn't have smart enough alias analyssis
to know what can/can't conflict.

Similarly, split the invert function into separate calculation/store calls,
so the inverse work can interleave better with the MMAs.

Move "solved" from sh_dh to sh_sh - reusing sh_dh needed a barrier but sh_sh
doesn't.

* interact properly with new replay code

</details>

<details open>

CUDA: cache the device type at init (#33142)

* CUDA: cache the device type at init

ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_type called cudaGetDeviceProperties on every
call, which takes ~0.7-1 ms with the CUDA 12 runtime. With tensor
overrides on multiple GPUs the scheduler queries the device type for every
split input, so this ran dozens of times per token.

Store the device type in ggml_cuda_device_info at init. It is derived from
prop.integrated, not from the integrated flag, which is forced off (#15034).

Ref #33132

* Apply suggestion from @JohannesGaessler

---------

Co-authored-by: Johannes Gäßler <johannesg@5d6.de>

</details>
